uncited: **Determine Slicing Direction (Base Plane):** Compute the viewing direction vector $\vec{v}$.
Calculate the angle between $\vec{v}$ and the three primary axes of the volume data (normals $\vec{n}_x, \vec{n}_y, \vec{n}_z$).
Select the axis with the minimum angle to the viewing direction as the "base plane" normal.
This determines which of the three texture stacks to use.
**Generate Slice Stack:** Define a set of parallel planes orthogonal to the viewing direction.
*Pre-computed Slices:* If slices are pre-computed orthogonal to a primary axis, they are stored as 2D textures.
*View-Aligned Slices:* For optimal quality, slices are generated orthogonal to the viewing direction for each frame.
*   **Sample Spacing:** Must be chosen to balance performance and quality.
*   **View Direction Parallel to Slices:** If the view direction is parallel to the primary axes of pre-computed slices, the projection distorts the slice views, degrading image quality.
*   **Popping Artifacts:** Sudden changes in slicing direction can cause popping.
